finding_groups.suggestion: The skill directs users to configure credentials via a local `.env` file and even references obtaining credentials from a named internal contact. finding_groups.suggestion: The skill exposes capabilities that affect external and local resources (network access to an Elasticsearch host, reading a local `.env` file, and writing output to arbitrary local paths) but does not declare any explicit tool scope, permissions, or allowed-tools metadata. In an agent execution context, that creates a least-privilege and transparency failure: the agent may be able to invoke this skill’s script without a clearly bounded capability declaration, even though the script can contact internal infrastructure, consume credentials, and write files. Add explicit skill-level permissions or an allowed-tools manifest describing: network access, file read of config/credential files, file write for output, and execution of the Python script. Scope the capabilities narrowly (e.g., only the configured ES host, only the skill directory for config, only an allowed output directory, and only read-only ES roles). If the platform supports capability review, declare it there and require user approval before first use.

finding_groups.message: The tool advertises support for relational query expressions such as `appId:"x" and message:"y" or traceId:"z"`, but `pa
finding_groups.suggestion: The tool advertises support for relational query expressions such as `appId:"x" and message:"y" or traceId:"z"`, but `parse_query_string()` only extracts `field:value` pairs and discards the boolean operators (`and`, `or`). Every extracted pair is then placed into an Elasticsearch `bool.filter` list, which enforces conjunctive (AND) semantics. Therefore an intended OR query silently becomes an AND query, causing false-negative results. In a production log-analysis or incident-response context, this can mislead analysts into believing no relevant events exist when they do. Implement a query parser that preserves boolean operators and precedence. At minimum, document that only AND semantics are supported. If OR is required, map OR conditions to Elasticsearch `bool.should` clauses and AND conditions to `bool.must`, and reject unsupported syntax instead of silently changing query semantics.

finding_groups.suggestion: The declared purpose is essentially a log-query helper, but the actual behavior appears to include network calls to an internal Elasticsearch endpoint, loading credentials from `.env`, issuing basic-auth requests, writing arbitrary local output files, and implicitly applying hardcoded internal defaults such as index and app IDs. This is a significant description-behavior mismatch because it understates the security and operational blast radius of the skill. Even if some details appear later in the markdown, the high-level capability model is still unsafe for an agent skill that touches production data. Rewrite the description and documentation to explicitly disclose all real behaviors: outbound network access to an internal ES host, credential handling from `.env`, basic auth usage, local file writes, and default targets. Replace implicit hardcoded internal defaults with explicit configuration. Require user confirmation before contacting production infrastructure, and document that the skill can read sensitive credentials and export potentially sensitive logs.

findings.message: MCP Tool Poisoning: The declared purpose is essentially a log-query helper, but the actual behavior appears to include network calls to an i
findings.suggestion: The declared purpose is essentially a log-query helper, but the actual behavior appears to include network calls to an internal Elasticsearch endpoint, loading credentials from `.env`, issuing basic-auth requests, writing arbitrary local output files, and implicitly applying hardcoded internal defaults such as index and app IDs. This is a significant description-behavior mismatch because it understates the security and operational blast radius of the skill. Even if some details appear later in the markdown, the high-level capability model is still unsafe for an agent skill that touches production data. Rewrite the description and documentation to explicitly disclose all real behaviors: outbound network access to an internal ES host, credential handling from `.env`, basic auth usage, local file writes, and default targets. Replace implicit hardcoded internal defaults with explicit configuration. Require user confirmation before contacting production infrastructure, and document that the skill can read sensitive credentials and export potentially sensitive logs.

findings.message: The skill facilitates access to production Elasticsearch logs and supports large exports to local files, but it does not
findings.suggestion: The skill facilitates access to production Elasticsearch logs and supports large exports to local files, but it does not warn that production logs may contain sensitive data (PII, tokens, secrets, internal identifiers, business data), that exported files may persist that data on disk, or that file output can overwrite existing files. In a production-debugging context, that omission materially increases the risk of accidental data exposure or data destruction. Add clear warnings that query results may contain sensitive data and must be handled securely. Require or default to safe output handling: path allow-listing, no overwriting without confirmation, append/random suffixes, restricted file permissions, and retention warnings. If feasible, add PII/secret redaction, field allow-lists, or sample-mode limiting for exploratory queries.

findings.message: The skill directs users to configure credentials via a local `.env` file and even references obtaining credentials from
findings.suggestion: The skill directs users to configure credentials via a local `.env` file and even references obtaining credentials from a named internal contact. That workflow has obvious credential-handling and privacy implications, but the documentation provides no warnings about storing secrets securely, restricting file permissions, avoiding secret leakage into logs/chat, or verifying the identity of the contact process. This is especially risky because the target system is production. Add explicit credential-handling guidance: keep `.env` out of version control, chmod 600, do not paste passwords into agent prompts or logs, use a secret manager or environment injection where possible, and ensure the ES account is least-privilege/read-only. Remove or generalize named internal contacts in favor of an approved ticketing or self-service flow to avoid informal credential distribution.

findings.message: The tool advertises support for relational query expressions such as `appId:"x" and message:"y" or traceId:"z"`, but `pa
findings.suggestion: The tool advertises support for relational query expressions such as `appId:"x" and message:"y" or traceId:"z"`, but `parse_query_string()` only extracts `field:value` pairs and discards the boolean operators (`and`, `or`). Every extracted pair is then placed into an Elasticsearch `bool.filter` list, which enforces conjunctive (AND) semantics. Therefore an intended OR query silently becomes an AND query, causing false-negative results. In a production log-analysis or incident-response context, this can mislead analysts into believing no relevant events exist when they do. Implement a query parser that preserves boolean operators and precedence. At minimum, document that only AND semantics are supported. If OR is required, map OR conditions to Elasticsearch `bool.should` clauses and AND conditions to `bool.must`, and reject unsupported syntax instead of silently changing query semantics.

findings.message: The code documentation explicitly implies support for relational expression parsing, including `or`, but the implementat
findings.suggestion: The code documentation explicitly implies support for relational expression parsing, including `or`, but the implementation ignores logical operators entirely and converts all parsed filters into conjunctive conditions. This is an intent-code divergence that can produce incorrect investigative results. Align documentation and implementation. Either update the docstring to state that only AND filters are supported, or implement real boolean expression parsing.

findings.message: MCP Least Privilege: The skill exposes capabilities that affect external and local resources (network access to an Elasticsearch host, readin
findings.suggestion: The skill exposes capabilities that affect external and local resources (network access to an Elasticsearch host, reading a local `.env` file, and writing output to arbitrary local paths) but does not declare any explicit tool scope, permissions, or allowed-tools metadata. In an agent execution context, that creates a least-privilege and transparency failure: the agent may be able to invoke this skill’s script without a clearly bounded capability declaration, even though the script can contact internal infrastructure, consume credentials, and write files. Add explicit skill-level permissions or an allowed-tools manifest describing: network access, file read of config/credential files, file write for output, and execution of the Python script. Scope the capabilities narrowly (e.g., only the configured ES host, only the skill directory for config, only an allowed output directory, and only read-only ES roles). If the platform supports capability review, declare it there and require user approval before first use.
